# Puṇṇakamāṇavapucchā (Snp 5.4 (PTS Snp 199))

**ID:** Snp 5.4 (PTS Snp 199)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Puṇṇakamāṇavapucchā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Puṇṇakamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Puṇṇaka") constitutes the fourth discourse of the *Pārāyanavagga* in the *Suttanipāta*, beginning at verse 1043 [Anderson & Smith 1913; Norman 1997–2001; Saddhatissa 2013]. In this dialogue, the young student Puṇṇaka approaches the Buddha with questions [Anderson & Smith 1913; Hazra 1994]. The Buddha explains that ascetics, monarchs (*khattiya*s), and brahmins who offer ritual sacrifices do so out of longing for sensual pleasures and worldly praise; because they are bound to these desires, sacrificial rites cannot enable them to cross beyond birth and old age [Hazra 1994]. Overcoming birth and decay is achieved instead through training the mind to transcend perturbation.

Curated passage-level parallels noted in canonical literature include the *Ānandasutta* (AN 3.32) and the *Samādhibhāvanāsutta* (AN 4.41).
